source: Monthly weather-sensitivity weights (0..1) for US production, Jan..Dec; field crops peak in their reproductive stage per USDA NASS Agricultural Handbook 628, Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates for U.S. Field Crops (2010) and USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook; livestock and manufactured goods are flat 1.0 (heat and drought hit pasture and feed year-round; manufactured goods are excluded from weather damage by the engine). Modeled, not measured.

eggs.source: flat 1.0: layer flocks are housed year-round; heat and drought act through feed cost and barn heat in every month

chicken.source: flat 1.0: broiler flocks turn over every 6-7 weeks; no seasonal crop stage

beef.source: flat 1.0: pasture and feed are hit by drought and heat in every month (ERS Livestock, Dairy and Poultry Outlook; 2012 herd liquidation)

pork.source: flat 1.0: confinement production; feed-cost channel is year-round

milk.source: flat 1.0: fluid milk tracks farm milk; dairy herds are housed year-round

milk-farm.source: flat 1.0: dairy herds produce every month; summer heat stress and feed cost are not crop-stage effects

cheese.source: flat 1.0: manufactured; excluded from weather damage elsewhere, kept flat here

bread.source: flat 1.0: manufactured; excluded from weather damage elsewhere, kept flat here

infant-formula.source: flat 1.0: manufactured; excluded from weather damage elsewhere, kept flat here

fats-oils.source: flat 1.0: manufactured; excluded from weather damage elsewhere, kept flat here

energy.source: flat 1.0: input, not a crop; flat

fertilizer.source: flat 1.0: input, not a crop; flat

corn.source: USDA NASS Agricultural Handbook 628, Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates for U.S. Field Crops (2010): corn planted Apr 20-Jun 5, silking Jul, harvested Sep 25-Nov 20; reproductive stage (Jul-Aug) is the yield-critical window (2012 analogue); USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook

soybeans.source: USDA NASS Agricultural Handbook 628, Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates for U.S. Field Crops (2010): soybeans planted May 5-Jun 20, pod fill Jul-Sep, harvested Sep 25-Nov 10; pod set and fill (Jul-Sep) decide yield; USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook

wheat.source: USDA NASS Agricultural Handbook 628, Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates for U.S. Field Crops (2010): winter wheat (about 70% of US output) planted Sep-Oct, jointing-heading-grain fill Apr-Jun, harvested Jun-Jul; spring wheat planted Apr-May, heading and fill Jun-Jul; blended by class share; USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook

rice.source: USDA NASS Agricultural Handbook 628, Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates for U.S. Field Crops (2010): rice planted Mar 25-May 25 (AR, CA, LA, MS, MO, TX), heading and grain fill Jun-Aug, harvested Aug-Oct; USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook

potatoes.source: USDA NASS Agricultural Handbook 628, Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates for U.S. Field Crops (2010): fall potatoes (ID, WA) planted Apr-May, tuber bulking Jun-Aug, harvested Sep-Oct; USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook

sugar.source: USDA NASS Agricultural Handbook 628, Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates for U.S. Field Crops (2010): sugarbeets planted Apr-May, root growth Jun-Sep, harvested Sep-Oct (MN, ND, ID); sugarcane (FL, LA) grows year-round and is harvested Oct-Mar; USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook

lettuce.source: USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook vegetables and pulses outlook: Salinas/Central Coast CA supplies Apr-Oct (main season, about 70% of volume), Yuma AZ and Imperial CA supply Nov-Mar; year-round floor 0.6

fresh-vegetables.source: USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook vegetables and pulses outlook: national field vegetable harvest peaks May-Sep, winter production concentrated in CA, AZ and FL; year-round floor 0.6

tomatoes.source: USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook vegetables and pulses outlook: CA processing tomatoes planted Feb-Jun and harvested Jul-Oct, fresh-market field tomatoes May-Sep; FL winter crop Dec-Mar carries a freeze risk (0.3)

apples.source: USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook fruit and tree nuts outlook: bloom and frost risk Apr-May (WA, NY, MI), fruit set and sizing Jun-Sep, harvest Sep-Oct; dormant Nov-Feb

citrus.source: USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook fruit and tree nuts outlook: Dec-Feb freeze season is the historic loss window (FL 1989, CA 2007); bloom, fruit set and summer growth 0.5

coffee.source: imported crop (Brazil, Colombia, Vietnam) with continuous harvest across origins; flat 1.0; USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook

bananas.source: imported crop (Guatemala, Ecuador, Costa Rica) harvested continuously; flat 1.0; USDA ERS crop calendars / production outlook
